scope: Opt-in native kernel bootstrap, per-transition USB object/topology matching, fresh reconnect instances; offline only
default_activation: Disabled. Explicit bootstrap_mode and per-device request required; no autoload aliases.
reconnect: Fresh passive 100a instance when USB core assigns the free interface; new explicit request required. Existing xpad owner unchanged.

full_regression.report_metadata_refresh: tests/run_startup_test.py rerun successfully after correcting stale report scope text

kernel_adapter.method: Actual extracted kernel C functions; synthetic USB tree, enumeration, ownership, workqueue, time and syscalls
kernel_adapter.coverage: PASS: 55 actual-kernel adapter scenarios; captured 15-TX bootstrap, arbitrary root/hub ports, handover permission/race, signal/disconnect/deadline/transfer failures, parallel reservation isolation, balanced refs, one-shot runtime sequence
limits: Does not execute Linux USB/input/IIO cores or real kernel locks/URBs.
Probe allocation/registration is simulated; the actual full module is built and analyzed separately.
No proof of race freedom, cold-start hardware success or suspend/resume support.

portable_startup.method: Actual shared C startup state machine; synthetic clock/transport/port ownership. Two recorded segments are joined synthetically, not a new capture.
portable_startup.coverage: PASS: 15 captured TX packets; 75 per-transfer failures; identity, ownership, pacing, deadlines, cancellation, idle-pad liveness, independent IMU, one-shot sequence handoff, four arbitrary topology tokens, two concurrent dongles, port moves and new reconnect sessions
limits: No live USB or kernel lifecycle executed.
This shared-core test excludes the kernel coordinator and activation interface; see kernel-startup-test.json for their separate simulation.
Returned TX intents do not open, claim, write, bind or initialize actual hardware.
READY marks completed init USB transfers and fresh raw IMU; firmware acknowledgement and gamepad evidence are separate.
Topology tokens simulate arbitrary root/hub ports; this test does not execute live Linux topology discovery or token allocation.
Gyroscope scale and physical axes remain uncalibrated.

native_motor_send.method: Actual gsn_sequence/gsn_fault/gsn_send/gsn_stop/gsn_flush_motors extracted unchanged; own shared C runtime and protocol; synthetic clock/locks/USB
cases: expiry between flush and send emits zero instead of restarting pulse
expired session cannot send a new motor packet
explicit stop emits zero and successful END does not duplicate it
USB transport error faults runtime and cannot report success
short USB transfer faults runtime and cannot report success
failed final stop is retained without retry or false success
invalid internal send shapes do not reach USB
clean unexpired state does not resend motor packet
maintenance and motor packets retain shared sequence
unbind blocks a new pulse but permits the final zero packet
limits: No real kernel lock scheduling, DMA, USB device, workqueue or concurrent IRQ execution.
Simulated clock jump covers expiry between flush and the final send gate; host scheduling after that gate is not a hard realtime guarantee.
USB replacement records requested bytes and injects completion results; no mechanical effect is measured.

static_analysis.limits: Static analysis does not model all kernel allocation/refcount/URB/workqueue concurrency semantics

open_items: No live cold start, USB core integration, mechanical action or return to xpad executed with this build.
Synthetic kernel-function tests do not prove real lock scheduling, race freedom, allocation failure handling or USB/input/IIO core behavior.
Different identical dongles at the same physical port within a pending transition are not authenticated by a verified stable UID.
Finite runtime retained: default 30 seconds, maximum 315 seconds. Permanent hotplug binding policy, suspend/resume restart and installation remain open.
No automatic retry or recovery after bootstrap failure; the future hardware run needs a concrete return plan and separate approvals.
Gyroscope physical scaling and calibrated SDL sensor output remain unresolved.
